<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XXIIII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|211}}</noinclude>backe from the monument, they told al these things to those eleuen, and to al the rest. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=10}}† And it vvas Marie Magdalene, and Ioane, and Marie of Iames, and the rest that vvere vvith them, vvhich said these things to the Apostles. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=11}}† And these vvordes seemed before them as dotage, and they did not beleeue them.

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=12}}† But {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 20, 3.''}}* Peter rising vp ranne to the monument: and stouping dovvne he savv the linnen clothes lying alone, and went avvay marueiling with him self at that which was done.

{{verse|chapter=24|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 16, 12.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Mr. 16, 12. · The Gospel vpō Munday in Easter weeke.}}∷ And behold, tvvo of them vvent the same day into a tovvne vvhich vvas the space of sixtie furlonges from Hierusalem, named Emmäùs. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=14}}† And they talked betwixt them selues of al those things that had chaunced. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=15}}† And it came to passe: vvhile they talked and reasoned {{sc|vvith}} them selues, IESVS also him self approching vvent vvith them. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=16}}† but their eies vvere held that they might not know him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=17}}† And he said to them, VVhat are these communications that you conferre one vvith an other vvalking, and are sad? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=18}}† And one vvhose name vvas Cleophas, ansvvering, said to him, Art thou only a stranger in Hierusalem, and hast not knovven the things that haue been done in it, these daies? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=19}}† To vvhom he said, VVhat things? And they said, concerning {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth, vvho vvas a man a Prophet, mightie in vvorke and vvorde before God and al the people. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=20}}† And hovv our cheefe Priestes and Princes deliuered him into condemnation of death, and crucified him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=21}}† but vve hoped that it vvas he that should redeeme Israel: and novv besides al this, to day is the third day since these things vvere done. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=22}}† But certaine vvomen also of ours, made vs afraid: vvho before it vvas light, vvere at the monument, {{verse|chapter=24|verse=23}}† and not finding his body, came, saying that they savv a vision also of Angels, vvho say that he is aliue. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=24}}† And certaine men of ours vvent to the monument: and they found it so as the vvomen said, but him they found not. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=25}}† And he said to them, O folish, and slovv of hart to beleeue, in al things vvhich the Prophets haue spoken. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=26}}† Ought not Christ to haue suffred these things, and so to enter into his glorie? {{verse|chapter=24|verse=27}}† And beginning from Moyses and al the Prophets, he did interpret to them in al the scriptures the things that vvere concerning him. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=28}}† And they drevv nigh to the tovvne vvhither they vvent: and he made semblaunce to goe further. {{verse|chapter=24|verse=29}}† And they forced<noinclude>{{rh||Dd ij|him,}}</noinclude>
